items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names in persisterRestore.ts (reconcileQueryState, usePersistedData) read clearly. The restore block inside Query.fetch has no comments, repeats the data fallback (`data.data !== undefined ? data.data : data.state?.data`) and uses `(value as any)[PERSISTER_RESTORE_RESULT_SYMBOL]`.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Restore is an inline block in fetch() calling this.setState, not a dedicated reducer action. Data fallback logic is duplicated in createPersisterRestoreResult and query.ts. fetchState gained a `state?: QueryState<any, any>` param, so restore concerns now touch every fetch.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: No normalisation of restored counts or timestamps: a Partial state is spread over this.state as-is. fetchState now keeps fetchFailureCount and error status on every new fetch (`state?.status === 'error' ? {error, status}`), which changes normal refetch behaviour beyond the restore case.

items.name: Restore path API contract
items.name_zh: 恢复路径 API 约定
items.evidence: Exported, symbol-branded marker that Query recognises; it returns before success callbacks and forces fetchStatus 'idle'. It is applied via setState rather than a dedicated restore action. The public signature uses `Partial<QueryState<any, any>>`, and it is unclear whether bulk restore shares one path.

items.name: Existing persister contract preserved
items.name_zh: 保持既有 persister 约定
items.evidence: New exports and the widened QueryPersister return type are additive, and the 42/42 P2P tests pass. However, the global fetchState change keeps the old failure count, and keeps status 'error' instead of 'pending' when a query with no data refetches. That shifts core behaviour for plain-data paths too.
